question: Under US federal law, what is the lowest hourly cash wage an employer may pay a waiter?
answer: $2.13, as long as tips make up the rest. Congress created this tipped minimum in 1966, and it has not risen since 1991, longer than the $7.25 frozen since 2009. The employer tops up only when tips fall short. In most states, part of a diner's tip pays the legal minimum.
move: Ask who actually pays a wage before crediting who signs the cheque.
reference: Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938, section 3(m)(2)(A), as amended in 1966 and 1996
